module_title: Expansion of British Power - Basic Understanding (Conquest of Bengal)
introduction: The East India Company, which initially came for trade, decided to establish an empire upon observing India's political weakness. The real expansion of British power began with the 'Conquest of Bengal' (Battles of Plassey and Buxar), which provided them with the immense wealth needed to conquer the rest of India.

core_concepts.title: Battle of Plassey (June 23, 1757)
core_concepts.description: Fought between Robert Clive (British) and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal. The British won without a real fight due to the betrayal of the Nawab's commander, Mir Jafar. It was more of a diplomatic conspiracy than a real battle.

core_concepts.title: Battle of Buxar (October 22, 1764)
core_concepts.description: Under the leadership of Hector Munro, the British army defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim (Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daula (Awadh), and Shah Alam II (Mughal Emperor). This was an actual military victory for the British.

core_concepts.title: Treaty of Allahabad (1765)
core_concepts.description: Signed between Robert Clive and the Mughal Emperor after the Battle of Buxar. It granted the British the 'Diwani' (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

core_concepts.title: Subsidiary Alliance
core_concepts.description: Introduced by Lord Wellesley, this was a system where Indian rulers had to keep a British army and a British Resident in their court. In return, the British promised to protect them from external attacks.

core_concepts.title: Doctrine of Lapse
core_concepts.description: An annexation policy introduced by Lord Dalhousie. According to this, if an Indian ruler died without a natural/biological male heir, they could not adopt a son, and their kingdom would be annexed into the British Empire.

important_entities.name: Robert Clive
important_entities.key_fact: Founder of the British Empire in India
important_entities.significance: Led the victory at Plassey and established the 'Dual Government' in Bengal.

important_entities.name: Siraj-ud-Daula
important_entities.significance: The Black Hole Tragedy (1756) occurred during his reign, which became a major catalyst for the Battle of Plassey.

important_entities.name: Lord Dalhousie
important_entities.significance: Annexed several states like Satara, Jhansi, and Nagpur into British India under the Doctrine of Lapse.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often consider Plassey as the establishment of British military power. In reality, Plassey was won through 'deceit'; the true establishment of British supremacy in India came from the military victory at the 'Battle of Buxar'.
While Lord Wellesley extensively applied the Subsidiary Alliance in India, the original brain behind this concept was the French Governor 'Dupleix'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: After Siraj-ud-Daula, Mir Jafar (a puppet) was made Nawab, followed by Mir Qasim (who rebelled). Finally, Mir Jafar was reinstated during the Battle of Buxar.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the exact years of the Battles of Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764), as well as the British commanders (Robert Clive, Hector Munro).
A frequent question: 'After which battle were Diwani rights granted?' (Answer: After the Battle of Buxar, via the Treaty of Allahabad).
